answer: Let a court, not a census, police identities. Anyone may stake a deposit to accuse a group of seats of sharing one operator, citing evidence like mirrored answers. A small jury drawn at random from staked graders rules; the loser may appeal, but each round doubles the jury size and the fee. A farm that buys a few jurors can't wander the case up to its zenith: the top court is so large and random that winning means bribing a crystal-clear majority of the whole pool, while honest accusers recover deposits plus the slashed seats.
